title: Feature Request: One change for the most important use of Notify Me
snippet: A key new feature in macOS 27 is Safari’s Notify Me function. This has the Apple Intelligence automatically monitor a web page for updates and send a notification when it occurs. This feature can be useful in a wide variety of ways, with price drops being one of the most obvious. Unfortunately, a limitation means that it doesn’t yet support what I would consider the most important use case for Notify Me … more…
fullText:
A key new feature in macOS 27 is Safari’s Notify Me function. This has the Apple Intelligence automatically monitor a web page for updates and send a notification when it occurs.

This feature can be useful in a wide variety of ways, with price drops being one of the most obvious. Unfortunately, a limitation means that it doesn’t yet support what I would consider the most important use case for Notify Me …

Given that computers were supposed to automate boring tasks so that humans didn’t have to do them, it’s somewhat disappointing just how frequently we find ourselves doing tedious and repetitive tasks that somehow can’t yet be easily automated. AI is changing this, and Apple’s Notify Me feature in Safari is a good example.

For example, if I’m waiting for a product to come back into stock in order to place an order, or delaying my purchase until the price drops to a more reasonable level, Safari can now monitor a web page and let me know when it’s time to buy.

But the single most tedious manual refreshing of websites I do on a regular basis is waiting for tickets to go on sale. There are some events that sell out within minutes of ticket sales opening, and as they frequently don’t happen exactly at the promised time, I often find myself visiting a website a few minutes before sales are supposed to begin and then repeatedly refreshing the page. 

In some cases, the sales window can open 20 or 30 minutes later than promised, so this process can grow extremely time-consuming and tedious. This is a perfect use case for the Notify Me feature.

Unfortunately, it can’t be used for this because the highest frequency check I can set is hourly. By the time Safari notifies me, there’s a high chance that all tickets would be sold out, or at least the ones for the seats that I really wanted.

I’d like one simple change: the ability to set the check frequency to every minute or even every 15 seconds.

I appreciate that people doing this for an extended period could effectively amount to a denial of service attack on a website, so Apple would have to impose limits on its use. A simple one would be to allow high-frequency checks to run for a maximum period of 30 minutes. Given that we wouldn’t typically need to check the same website very often, the company could even have a reset time of a month before we can use the feature again on the same website.

fullText:
Stevie Bonifield

 

is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

The new Fire TV Stick 4K will be a little easier to set up than Amazon’s previous 4K streaming sticks since it no longer requires a power adapter. You can power the device directly from your TV’s USB port, like the updated entry-level Fire TV Stick Amazon launched earlier this year. The Fire TV Stick 4K, available starting today for $59.99, runs on Amazon’s refreshed TV OS and includes Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, and Bluetooth Low Energy.

Amazon’s also simplifying its streaming stick lineup, which now includes four devices instead of five: the Fire TV Stick HD, Fire TV Stick 4K, Fire TV Stick 4K Max, and Fire TV Cube. The new Fire TV Stick 4K is replacing Amazon’s earlier “Select” and “Plus” 4K streaming sticks.

A redesigned Fire TV Remote is launching alongside the new streaming stick, featuring a new asymmetrical shape and “more tactile controls.” The new remote is compatible with all Amazon Ember TVs and Fire TV streaming devices from 2019 onward. It will be available standalone for $14.99 and starts shipping late October. Amazon says it also plans to launch a “Plus” version of the new remote early next year, with an aluminum design, backlit buttons, and a “Find My Remote” feature.

Fire TV is getting a few software updates, as well, including an Alexa Plus Hub and an Alexa Plus integration in the Fire TV mobile app. Amazon says its AI “now draws on real-world context” like awards and events, helping it answer more complex prompts for show and movie suggestions. Amazon Music is also getting a new Fire TV app later this fall, with an Alexa Plus integration users can prompt for music and podcast recommendations.

title: a16z-backed EliseAI raises $350M, doubles valuation to $4B
snippet: EliseAI raises $350M, doubles valuation in a year.
fullText:
In Brief

Image Credits:SophonK / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

AI startup EliseAI announced on Tuesday that it has raised $350 million at a $4 billion valuation, double what it was worth when it raised its Series E last August.

This latest round was co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer Ventures. EliseAI, founded in 2017, automates administrative and operational work for housing and healthcare companies. It said its software is used by one in six apartments across the country and announced this summer it passed $200 million in ARR. 

Earlier this month, EliseAI announced the launch of an AI “teammate” called Apollo that helps with tasks inside the EliseAI platform. “It’s built natively into the same platform that already runs leasing, maintenance, and renewals,” co-founder and CEO Minna Song told TechCrunch. “So it can act across every role on a property team.” 

EliseAI also helps automate the patient-related paperwork for specialty physician groups on the healthcare side, “from the first inbound call through referrals, scheduling, insurance verification, chart prep, and follow-up, so nothing falls through the cracks,” she said. The company has targeted housing and healthcare because they are two of the “largest expenses for American households,” she said.

title: OpenAI reportedly in talks to raise $30B round at $1.4T valuation
snippet: The new round is anticipated to be the company's last before its delayed 2027 public debut.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

12:52 PM PDT · September 29, 2026

Image Credits:Kyle Grillot/Bloomberg / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

OpenAI is in talks with investors to raise at least $30 billion in a pre-IPO funding round at a valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday.

Investors are eager to pour more funds into the ChatGPT maker ahead of its anticipated public market debut next year. While Anthropic momentarily outpaced OpenAI at the start of the year, recent strategic refocus on key areas like coding has fueled a 70% jump in run-rate revenue since July, reaching $40 billion in August, according to the report.

The company previously raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion valuation. That funding round was supposed to be its last private raise before an IPO, which had been, until recently, expected to take place this year. However, CEO Sam Altman has now ruled out a public debut in 2026 to prioritize AI safety first. 

“I think it is unacceptable to be taking like a 10% chance of killing everybody by the end of the decade,” he recently told Fortune, in response to warnings from safety researchers about AI posing an existential risk to humanity.

The new fundraising, if it transpires, will serve as a bridge round to the IPO, according to Bloomberg.

OpenAI didn’t respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

He said an API lets developers read the angle of the hinge with an accuracy of around five degrees, and the ability to read what Apple describes as the “pose” of the device …

Apple itself uses the hinge angle in a number of ways in software, including a feature that became an instant hit: the way the outer screen defocuses into a preview of the inner one as you open the phone. He told Donald Decodes that the feature is subtle but magical.

The goal was not a fancy animation you’d think about, but something you’d perceive automatically: the screen becomes translucent, a window to what’s below. Fundamental to the device is continuity between your experience when it’s closed and what you find when you open it. Seeing through the screen above to what’s about to be revealed below eases that journey in the most natural way. We’re really delighted with how it came out. It’s subtle but magical.

Federighi says he is confident that developers will do creative and exciting things with the hinge information exposed, just as they have with other iPhone data made available to them.

For most developers […] we’re focused on communicating the pose of the device: are you in book pose, on-table pose, tent pose? Developers don’t have to work with how many degrees open it is. By communicating the pose, the frameworks can react automatically and deliver a consistent experience across apps. But for creative experiences, like our own animation, developers can get closer to the raw information […]

We have a long history of exposing gyroscope and accelerometer data to developers, and they’ve made really interesting use of it over time. One of the ways this device expresses itself is through its poses and the hinge, and we’re excited to see what developers do with it.

He said Apple has also worked hard to make it easier for developers to create apps that take full advantage of the iPhone Duo’s capabilities.

We’ve built our platform on high-level frameworks like UIKit and SwiftUI that abstract away many of the harder layout problems, so apps often inherit new behaviors automatically. Over time we’ve added more high-level constructs that adapt automatically, which makes this transition nearly automatic for many developers.

He added that Apple also supports agentic coding tools to enable developers to adapt existing apps almost completely automatically. You can watch the interview below.

title: The internet is convinced Elon Musk’s xAI trolled OpenAI’s ‘Dots’ launch
snippet: Before OpenAI launched its new AI agent, Dots, on Tuesday, Elon Musk's xAI had already acquired the domain name "dot.com," which now redirects to the Grok chatbot download page.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

3:20 PM PDT · September 29, 2026

Image Credits:Sean Gallup / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

On Tuesday, OpenAI launched a new product called Dots, an always-on AI agent with a bubbly, blobby avatar. While the colorful avatar might evoke a smile, the biggest laugh from the launch is (we imagine) being had by Elon Musk, the former OpenAI founder who left, launched competitor Grok, and unsuccessfully sued.

That’s because the domain “dot.com” belongs to Musk’s xAI, and it currently redirects to the download page for xAI’s Grok chatbot app. According to the Whois domain owner registry, that domain name was just transferred in July.

It is entirely possible that xAI bought the domain for normal domain-buying reasons. “Dot” could be a typo of “bot,” so it nabbed it to grab mistyped searches. We’ve reached out to xAI and asked. But xAI doesn’t own the “bot.com” name, nor does it own other obvious typo domains like “vot.com,” which is listed for sale.

The internet’s theory is far funnier: that Musk (or his team) pulled off a prank, getting wind of OpenAI’s new product and its name and buying the domain name. 

In fact, anonymous X user and xAI watcher @birdabo (this person calls themselves “chief shitposting officer @SpaceXAI“) was first to spot the domain name in a now-viral post. Whatever the motivation, the circumstance is funny.

And as for the “dots.com” domain, a more direct fit to the product name, it currently belongs to a long-defunct company. So if a petty revenge prank was really the motivation, grabbing that name, too, would be next-level.

fullText:
9to5Mac is brought to you by CleanMyMac by MacPaw. With the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate, use CleanMyMac first to free up space, optimize your system, and ensure your new Mac runs at 100% on day one. Learn more.

Apple has released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public after several months of beta testing. The update is headlined by Siri AI, but there are also Apple Intelligence enhancements to many of Apple’s own Mac apps. Here are a few of my favorites.

Apple Intelligence in macOS 27 

One of the best things about Apple’s strategy with Apple Intelligence is how it sprinkles AI-powered features throughout system apps across all of its platforms. The Mac is a great example of this, and macOS 27 takes things up a notch.

Photos

In the Photos app, there are multiple new editing tools powered by Apple Intelligence. Spatial Reframing lets you change the perspective of an image after it’s been taken, while Extend lets you expand an image across its original edges. There’s also a more powerful version of Clean Up for removing objects and people from an image after the fact.

Safari

In Safari, Apple has added several new intelligence features. You can now automatically group your tabs by topics. Using the new Notify Me feature in Safari, you can get push notifications when changes are made to a website. This is great for tracking price changes or restocks of sold-out products.

Describe an Extension might be my favorite feature in macOS 27. It lets you create a custom extension for Safari just by using a natural language prompt.

Shortcuts

Shortcuts can be a powerful way to create automations on your Mac. In macOS 27, Apple has made the process of creating shortcuts much easier. You can now use natural language to describe the shortcut you want, and Shortcuts will automatically create it.

You can even iterate on that shortcut using natural language. You can also, of course, still manually create a shortcut.

Finder

Apple has even added new Apple Intelligence features to Finder on the Mac. When naming a fold or file, you can now get suggestions powered by Apple Intelligence. So based on the content of the document or file, macOS 27 will suggest a name.

Wrap up

macOS 27 is available to Mac users everywhere. The update is supported on all Apple Silicon-powered Macs.

What are your favorite macOS 27 features? Are you using any of these new Apple Intelligence features? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Google Health 5.09 rolling out: Cardio Load from third-party workouts, more
snippet: Following yesterday’s announcement, Google Health 5.09 is rolling out with support for the new Health Guardian features on the Pixel Watch. more…
fullText:
Following yesterday’s announcement, Google Health 5.09 is rolling out with support for the new Health Guardian features on the Pixel Watch.

With version 5.09 for Android, Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 users can set up blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics. The first monthly Health Guardian summary will appear at the beginning of October, while you can also find information in the Health tab afterwards:

Blood pressure trends, that allow you to track blood pressure patterns before they can put strain on your heart, will be available in the Heart section of the Health tab if you’ve worn your watch for 5 or more consecutive days in September.

Insulin resistance trends will be available in the Metabolic section of the Health tab if you’ve worn your watch for 7 or more days and nights in September.

Sleep breathing quality metrics, so you can learn how your sleep breathing patterns can affect your daily energy, will be available in the Sleep tab and Respiratory section of the Health tab. You’ll be able to see both daily and monthly trends.

There are also three other sets of improvements with Google Health 5.09 on Android and iOS:

	

Cardio Load for Workouts Started in Other Apps

	

Since launch, Google Health has allowed you to connect your favorite apps and devices to the Google Health experience. Now, the workouts you track in other apps and devices and sync to Google Health can count toward your Cardio Load, as long as the other app or device has tracked your heart rate data during that workout. This means workouts you track on other wearables like a Garmin or Apple Watch and sync to Google Health will earn Cardio Load.

Nutrition Improvements

When creating a custom food, you can now toggle food serving units and meal time more easily.

We’ve resolved an issue with custom food creation on iOS and fixed a bug where deleted items could still appear in your custom food list.

Activity and Fitness Updates

You now have more options for how you log your completed activities on the Fitness tab. Tap the “Log activity” button to see them all.

We’ve fixed an issue where some historical step streaks were missing. We are now restoring this data, and your missing streaks will reappear soon.”

title: Apple has big October coming for new hardware and software, here’s the lineup
snippet: Apple has a big October ahead, with several major hardware and software launches coming. Here’s everything to expect from Apple in October. more…
fullText:
Apple has a big October ahead, with several major hardware and software launches coming. Here’s everything to expect from Apple in October.

iPhone Duo launches October 23

iPhone Duo is confirmed to arrive in users’ hands in October. Pre-orders open Friday, October 16 and the first units deliver on October 23.

Apple’s first foldable model might be limited in supply. However, iPhone Duo is launching in lots of countries simultaneously, which could be a good sign for availability. Per Apple:

Customers in more than 70 countries and regions, including Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Colombia, France, Germany, India, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, Türkiye, the UAE, the UK, the U.S., and Vietnam, will be able to pre-order iPhone Duo beginning at 5 a.m. PT on Friday, October 16, with availability beginning Friday, October 23. iPhone Duo will be available in 28 other countries and regions beginning Friday, October 30.

If iPhone Duo supply was expected to be significantly lower than anticipated demand, it’s unlikely Apple would launch the product in close to 100 countries and regions right away.

Read more: Apple unveils foldable iPhone Duo

Hardware rumors: New Macs, Home products, and iPad mini

Apple reportedly has a lot more new hardware products launching in October too. We’re expecting new Macs, Home products, and an upgraded iPad mini. Here’s what’s rumored:

Touchscreen MacBook Pro / Ultra: All-new design for high-end MacBook with OLED, more

M6 iMac: Powerful chip and new color options

M6 MacBook Pro: Update for 14-inch base MacBook Pro

New Apple TV 4K: A19 or A19 Pro chip, Siri AI, new Siri Remote

HomePad: New home hub with built-in touchscreen

HomePod mini 2: More powerful chip, audio upgrades, more

iPad mini: OLED display, A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip

Two standout products include the first touchscreen Mac, which could be branded MacBook Pro or Ultra, and the long-expected home hub ‘HomePad.’ Everything else will be smaller updates to existing products.

Software launches: iOS 27.1 and iOS 27.2, more

Apple has confirmed that iPhone Duo will run on iOS 27.1 when it launches in October. 

It’s speculated that 27.1 will be Duo-exclusive. However, it might come to other iPhones too, but only include bug fixes or security updates while the majority of changes are for Apple’s foldable.

Normally we would expect more features in iOS 27.1, but in an unusual move, iOS 27.2 is already in testing and is also expected to arrive in October. As a result, iOS 27.2 is likely intended for all iPhones while 27.1 is primarily for iPhone Duo. 

New features in iOS 27.2 so far include:

Profiles for the Apple TV app come to iPhone and iPad

Dual Capture feature available for Group FaceTime calls

Siri AI expands to several new languages

New features for Apple Music, CarPlay Ultra, and more might be coming too

When iOS 27 launched, Apple confirmed that Siri AI “will expand to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish next month.“ Since that language expansion is included in iOS 27.2, we’re expecting both 27.1 and 27.2 to arrive before October ends.

The iOS 27.2 beta also includes an all-new Health app with Apple Intelligence features, but it’s expected to be removed from the shipping version and return in iOS 27.3 later this year instead.

Read more: Here’s everything new Apple TV has coming in October

fullText:
Since the Galaxy Tab S10 line, Samsung has updated its flagship Ultra tablet annually, but alternates its regular and Plus variants. It means that this year’s Galaxy Tab S12 series includes an Ultra model with few changes from last year’s Tab S11 Ultra, and a Plus variant that brings a bigger overhaul to the two-year-old Tab S10 Plus. There’s no regular Tab S12, suggesting fans of the smaller size will have to wait until 2027 for the next version of that tablet.

The Galaxy Tab S12 Plus should be a meaningful update to owners of the Tab S10 Plus or older. Compared to that tablet, it has a slightly larger and brighter 12.6-inch display, despite running thinner and lighter overall. The MediaTek Dimensity 9500 chipset is two generations ahead of the old 9300 Plus, and the 10,600mAh battery is bigger too. It’s all enough to make the $200 cost increase, to a new starting price of $1,199, feel worthwhile.

By contrast, the Tab S12 Ultra is altogether more familiar, though only because it benefited from those design upgrades last year. Compared to the Tab S11 Ultra, the only real changes are the annual chipset bump and upgraded four-channel spatial audio (also found on the Plus). The Ultra’s 14.6-inch display, 11,600mAh battery, and 5.1mm-thick design are all unchanged year-on-year. That would be easier to swallow if it didn’t also come at a $200 premium, now $1,399.

1/3The Ultra still has a small notch for its selfie camera, though the Plus model places it inside the bezel. Image: Samsung

Both tablets benefit from bright OLED displays with 1,600 nits of peak brightness, IP68 ratings, and seven years of Android updates. An S Pen stylus comes in the box, as does a welcome software update: the Android debut of Adobe Photoshop for Tablets, which will be a Galaxy Store exclusive for six months. It comes with Adobe’s AI features, a tablet-optimized interface, and support for the S Pen.

The Galaxy Tab S12 Plus and Tab S12 Ultra will hit shelves on October 7th.

title: iOS 27.2: Three new features coming soon to your iPhone
snippet: iOS 27.0.1 just launched yesterday, but Apple is already well on its way to preparing iOS 27.2 as a forthcoming iPhone update (with 27.1 likely iPhone Duo-only). Here are three new features coming with iOS 27.2. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.0.1 just launched yesterday, but Apple is already well on its way to preparing iOS 27.2 as a forthcoming iPhone update (with 27.1 likely iPhone Duo-only). Here are three new features coming with iOS 27.2.

#1: Dual Capture for Group FaceTime

FaceTime got one of its biggest upgrades in years with iOS 27. 

On compatible iPhone models, Dual Capture lets you display both your front and rear camera views at the same time. Just tap the ‘Flip’ button and the back camera will go live while the front camera remains active.

And in iOS 27.2, the feature gets even better by adding support for Group FaceTime calls.

iOS 27 currently only lets you use Dual Capture in one-on-one calls, but with iOS 27.2 it will be available for Group FaceTime too.

#2: Apple Podcasts overhauls ‘Up Next’ queue

Apple Podcasts gets a key change in iOS 27.2 that I’m already a big fan of in the beta.

The previous ‘Up Next’ queue at the top of the app’s Home tab is being split into two new sections:

New Episodes replaces Up Next, and contains the latest releases for shows you follow

Continue Playing is brand new, located directly below New Episodes as a hub for all in-progress shows

I’ve criticized the Up Next feature before for being cluttered and confusing, so I’m very excited to see this change. In my early testing, I think it’s a huge improvement that helps users better keep track of everything they’re listening to.

#3: Apple TV app supports user profiles

Apple’s TV app is about to support user profiles on iPhone, bringing the feature over from tvOS to iOS for the first time.

When you first launch the TV app in iOS 27.2, you’ll see a new profile selection screen. You can easily disable it from ever showing up again. But if your child ever watches videos on your iPhone, you might be very glad about this new feature.

With profiles, the Apple TV app can change which content it displays and recommends based on the selected viewer. And importantly, when a child’s profile is active, they’ll only see age-appropriate series and movies from Apple. So not only does your own personal viewing queue stay uncluttered, but you also ensure your child doesn’t see something they shouldn’t.

title: Samsung’s Galaxy SmartTag 3 works with iPhones, but not Android Find Hub
snippet: Samsung has announced its Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a new AirTag rival with an updated design, longer battery life, and support for iPhone users. more…
fullText:
Samsung has announced its Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a new AirTag rival with an updated design, longer battery life, and support for iPhone users.

In a press release today, Samsung unveiled the Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a “smaller, lighter” tracker. Specifically, it’s 35% smaller and 33% lighter. It shrinks down by ditching the built-in mounting loop, instead relying on add-on cases and accessories to connect to other objects. Samsung says the tracker has 550 days of battery life in typical use and up to 790 in “Power Saving Mode,” while also supporting both Bluetooth 6.0 with channel sounding and UWB for precise finding.

Galaxy SmartTag 3 integrates with the Galaxy Find Network which is available on Galaxy smartphones and usable through the SmartThings Find app. Samsung touts over 900 million Galaxy devices building out the network.

New this time around, too, is support for tracking down a SmartTag 3 via iPhone. Samsung’s app on iPhone supports finding the tracker, though it doesn’t contribute to the network. Still rather handy for families with multiple types of devices.

	

While iPhone support has been added, Samsung’s new tracker still doesn’t integrate with the wider Android Find Hub network which works across all Android devices rather than only Galaxy.

Other new features include:

Place Notification… adds a proactive layer, letting users define an area and receive an alert when a tagged item moves in or out of it.

Location History lets users review where their tag has been

Movement Detection Alert can notify them when movement is detected so they can stay informed without actively checking.

NFC-powered Lost Mode, which can display registered contact information or a short message when a lost tag is scanned with a compatible mobile device.

SmartThings IoT Control, which allows users to trigger preset routines for compatible connected devices using the tag button.

Left Behind Alert, which can notify users when their mobile device loses connection with a tagged belonging.

The Galaxy SmartTag 3 will be available on October 7, the same date as Samsung’s new Galaxy Tab S12 series.

title: Fake iPhone Duo preorder page can steal crypto wallet data and more
snippet: iPhone Duo pre-orders start on Friday, October 16, but scammers are trying to trick people into visiting a fake website to place their order now. The website with the malware convincingly replicates the look of the real thing and claims to offer a $500 discount voucher as an “Authorized Partner Exclusive” … more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo pre-orders start on Friday, October 16, but scammers are trying to trick people into visiting a fake website to place their order now.

The website with the malware convincingly replicates the look of the real thing and claims to offer a $500 discount voucher as an “Authorized Partner Exclusive” … 

Security researchers at Malwarebytes say the page uses the DarkSword exploit chain, which works with some older unpatched iPhones. You don’t have to do anything, just visiting the page is enough for the attack to launch.

Behind its Apple-style design and $500 voucher, the page uses the leaked DarkSword exploit chain to try to break into vulnerable iPhones. If it succeeds, a separate payload attempts to steal saved credentials, cryptocurrency wallet data, and notes. You don’t have to fill in the form, tap a download, or approve anything. Opening the page is enough to start the attempt.

If it succeeds, then it captures your device identifier information and status and attempts to send a list of installed apps and the contents of your Apple Notes. Having done this, it turns its attention to crypto wallets.

The code looks for cryptocurrency wallets, including MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet, Coinbase Wallet, Exodus, and Tonkeeper. It also attempts to recover saved credentials from the phone’s keychain. If it finds a targeted wallet and the first exchanges with its server succeed, it attempts to upload wallet files, recovered keychain data, and photo thumbnails. Exposure of wallet files or credentials could put funds at risk.

It goes on to try to access messages, contacts, call history, voicemail, email, calendar entries, and cached location data. The payload can also contact its server for further instructions. 

The exploit chain was disclosed by Google back in March, with Apple issuing a patch later the same month. 

9to5Mac’s Take

The usual advice applies to protect yourself. Never visit links sent to you unless you trust the sender and are specifically expecting them. Always ensure that you install iOS updates as soon as they are available.

title: Apple’s Taptic Engine patent defeat sends litigation funder’s shares up 9%
snippet: Shares in litigation funder Burford Capital jumped more than 9% today as a result of Apple’s $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Shares in litigation funder Burford Capital jumped more than 9% today as a result of Apple’s $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement. Here are the details.

Apple verdict lifts litigation funder valuation

Last Friday, a US jury ruled that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes on two patents held by California-based company Taction Technology.

Apple introduced the Taptic Engine in September 2014 with the first Apple Watch, and the technology has since expanded to other products, including the iPhone, where it provides haptic feedback for notifications, interactions, and other system events.

When Taction filed its patent infringement lawsuit in 2021, the company accused Apple of directly and indirectly infringing two of its patents through the Taptic Engine used in a range of iPhone and Apple Watch models.

Last Friday, following the verdict, Taction said the jury had “vindicated its patent rights,” while Apple said it strongly disagreed with the decision and would appeal.

Earlier today, as reported by The Financial Times, litigation funder Burford Capital disclosed that it has a financial entitlement in the case, and that it could be entitled to $1.4 billion if the $5.7 billion verdict is ultimately paid in full.

The disclosure sent Burford shares sharply higher in London, with the stock closing up 9.41% and giving the company a market capitalization of £659.9 million, or roughly $875 million.

Bloomberg Law notes that court records show that Taction received funding from Kenosha Investments LP and Gronostaj Investments LLC. The report also notes that Kenosha has been identified as an indirect subsidiary of Burford, which finances lawsuits in exchange for a share of any eventual recovery.

In a statement to investors on Monday, Burford said that if the $5.7 billion verdict were paid in full, its $1.4 billion entitlement would be split roughly equally between the company’s own balance sheet and its investment funds.

title: Apple faces class action over Apple Pay fees charged to card issuers
snippet: U.S. District Judge Jeffrey S. White has certified a class-action lawsuit accusing Apple of charging payment card issuers inflated fees for Apple Pay transactions. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
U.S. District Judge Jeffrey S. White has certified a class-action lawsuit accusing Apple of charging payment card issuers inflated fees for Apple Pay transactions. Here are the details.

As first spotted by AppleInsider, a federal judge has allowed an antitrust lawsuit over Apple Pay fees to proceed as a class action, meaning payment card issuers across the U.S. may now pursue their claims against Apple as a group.

In a press release from Hagens Berman, the law firm representing the plaintiffs, the firm said the certified class includes all U.S. entities that issued payment cards enabled for Apple Pay and paid Apple fees on transactions made with those cards.

The firm argues that while mobile wallets on Android do not charge card issuers transaction fees, Apple charges U.S. issuers 0.15% on credit card transactions and 0.5 cents on debit card transactions made through Apple Pay.

From the press release:

The lawsuit accuses Apple of extracting up to $1 billion annually in fees in violation of federal antitrust law. Apple denies rivals access to the technology needed to develop a competing mobile wallet, according to the class action. On iOS devices, Apple has ensured that only its mobile wallet, Apple Pay, can make contactless payments at the point of sale. Having secured a monopoly for Apple Pay in this fashion, Apple charges card issuers who use Apple Pay, like credit unions and other small financial institutions, supracompetitive fees for a service that is available on Android devices for free, according to the lawsuit.

The firm also highlighted that Judge White “denied Apple’s motion to exclude expert testimony attorneys say establishes common proof that Apple maintains monopoly power in a relevant antitrust aftermarket for tap-and-pay iOS mobile wallets as well as a broader market for all mobile wallets.”

The lawsuit seeks reimbursement for card issuers that paid Apple Pay fees, as well as an injunction against Apple’s challenged policies.

title: Google Pixel 11A Leak May Have Revealed a New Color and Spec Bumps
snippet: The purported renders show a similar design to the Pixel 10A, but this time with the newest Tensor chip.
fullText:
Google’s next lower-cost flagship phone, the Pixel 11A, appears to have been leaked for the first time through a series of renders posted on Tuesday by Android Headlines and OnLeaks.

The images suggest that the Pixel 11A will come in a new purple color, but otherwise continue to have a simple flat design without a camera bump — much like the $499 Pixel 10A. That purple color would join black, silver and green variants, all of which will likely get renamed with something artsy from Google’s marketing department in due time.

While the design might be the same, the Pixel 11A is apparently expected to get the Tensor G6 processor — the same as the one in Google’s $899 Pixel 11. If this pans out, that’d be great to see, since the prior Pixel 10A used the same Tensor G4 processor as the Pixel 9 series. And while I did find in my Pixel 10A review that the phone was still feature-packed with one of the best cameras out there for its price range, it notably did not have access to several Pixel 10 features like Magic Cue for contextual assistance.

			

More from CNET

Google didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

The Pixel 11A is likely still months away from an official unveiling; for reference, the Pixel 10A was announced in February. 

It’s also unknown how the ongoing RAM shortage would affect the initial pricing for Pixel’s A-series. While the Pixel 7A through 10A also started at $499, it would not be surprising to see the Pixel 11A get its starting price bumped up to $599, much like the rest of the Pixel 11 lineup. If that happens, hopefully it follows the cue of the base Pixel 11 by simply eliminating the $499 128GB model while retaining a 256GB model at $599 — much like the current Pixel 10A.

title: Even Google Search agrees that ‘Googlebook’ wasn’t a very good name choice
snippet: “Googlebook” is a weird name, right? That was my personal first takeaway from this new platform, and it seems even Google Search supports the idea that Google should have used something else, as you can’t actually search for “Googlebook” without getting redirected elsewhere. more…
fullText:
“Googlebook” is a weird name, right? That was my personal first takeaway from this new platform, and it seems even Google Search supports the idea that Google should have used something else, as you can’t actually search for “Googlebook” without getting redirected elsewhere.

“Googlebook” is the name of Google’s new Android-based laptop platform, while “Google Books” is the company’s long-running index of books. 

See the problem? 

	

As pointed out by The Verge late last week, searching for “Googlebooks” on Google Search currently directs to a “Did you mean?” search for “Google Books.” You have to then manually click a link to actually search for Googlebook laptops. 

	

This is still happening as of today.

Searching for “Googlebook” doesn’t return the same error, but it’s a pretty funny result for Google’s own platform.

title: Final Cut Camera updated with support for iPhone 18 Pro features, more
snippet: Apple is rolling out a big update to Final Cut Camera today, the pro video app it first released for iPhone back in 2024. The update introduces a new design along with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro. more…
fullText:
Apple is rolling out a big update to Final Cut Camera today, the pro video app it first released for iPhone back in 2024. The update introduces a new design along with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro.

For those unfamiliar, Apple touts Final Cut Camera as a way to “record professional videos with full control of your footage and connect to Final Cut Pro for iPad to capture multiple angles at once with Live Multicam.” Apple announced the app in May 2024 and released it a month later.

Final Cut Camera version 2.4 is rolling out today with multiple key changes. First, it introduces a new, more customizable design with easier access to different settings.

The update also adds support for iPhone 18 Pro’s variable aperture, from f/1.48 to f/4, including shutter priority, aperture priority, and manual modes. It also supports Cinematic mode effects on iPhone 18 Pro, including video shot in ProRes and Apple Log.

With iPhone 18 Pro, users can take advantage of the new Fusion Main camera with variable aperture — the most advanced camera Apple has ever made — which brings aperture control to iPhone for the first time. Final Cut Camera allows creators to precisely dial in their aperture settings, or choose between shutter priority and aperture priority modes, to record stunning videos. The update also unlocks Cinematic mode effects for regular video, including footage captured in ProRes and Apple Log, allowing creators to adjust focus points and depth of field while editing in Final Cut Pro.

You can download Final Cut Camera on the App Store. The new update will start rolling out today. The app requires a subscription to Apple Creator Studio, which is $12.99 per month or $129 per year.

title: OpenAI cancels GPT-6.1 Astra release over misbehavior & safety concerns
snippet: OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving. more…
fullText:
OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving.

The New York Times reports that OpenAI was planning to release GPT-6.1 Astra “in the coming days or weeks,” sometime in October, as its next major model release. GPT-6 Astra launched on September 3. GPT-6.1 Astra is said to have been “more capable” compared to GPT-6 in “completing challenging tasks from end-to-end without human assistance, as well as writing.”

The report cites an interview with Saachi Jain, OpenAI’s head of safety systems, who confirmed that the model had regressed in two specific areas. Firstly, it “performed poorly on tests measuring alignment,” or how closely it sticks to the commands/prompts given by the human operator. Secondly, it showed “higher levels of deception,” not always telling the truth about the actions it did or did not take following a prompt. It was also added that GPT-6.1 Astra would push forward in a task beyond the current scope and without user permission, including interacting with external tools and/or services.

The new model would have been available in both ChatGPT and Codex.

	

OpenAI is due to have its annual developer conference, DevDay, tomorrow, where it’s very possible the company may have teased this new model update. Instead, the report explains, OpenAI will shift focus to “improving the safety of future models.”

This comes at a time when both OpenAI and Anthropic are calling for a slowdown in major AI development following recent breaches in GPT and Claude. Google’s Gemini also hacked into companies like those models, but stopped those actions faster than either of its rivals.

title: Google rolling out blood pressure & insulin resistance, more on Pixel Watch 3, 4, 5
snippet: As previewed during last month’s Pixel Watch 5 launch, Google is now starting to roll out blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics. more…
fullText:
As previewed during last month’s Pixel Watch 5 launch, Google is now starting to roll out blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics.

Health Guardian is Google’s overarching brand for the Pixel Watch’s suite of “proactive health and safety tools.” It includes Breathing Emergency Detection, which is available in Europe on the Pixel Watch 4 and 5.

The blood pressure trends feature works by passively measuring your pulse and motion patterns over the course of a month. It’s intended to let you detect “persistent higher cardiovascular trends early.” This works without a cuff or manual calibration, and was trained using billions of minutes of raw heart and movement data. You need “at least 5 consecutive days in a week” of data.

Insulin resistance trends analyze multi-week physiological data to track shifts in metabolic health without requiring a blood draw. Insulin resistance impacts how your body absorbs energy from food, with Google needing a minimum of 7 days of data in a month. The feature uses Google’s largest sensor foundational model. It was pre-trained using over 1 trillion minutes of data from 5 million opted-in users.

	
	

Both sets of trend insights will appear in the Google Health app on the first day of each month.

Meanwhile, sleep breathing quality metrics will track overnight breathing changes. In the morning, you’ll see how much time was spent optimally breathing, while a monthly report identifies longer-term patterns.

Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 users will be able to set up these three features in the Google Health app starting this week. Access is free on those three devices, with the first trend reports coming in early October.

If you’re a Google Health Premium subscriber, these three features are also coming to the Fitbit Air “later this year.”

title: Samsung’s Android 17 floodgates are open – updates rolling out for Galaxy S26, S25, more
snippet: The floodgates are open. After a delay and staggered starts, Samsung is widely rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users around the globe, and they’re not alone. more…
fullText:
The floodgates are open. After a delay and staggered starts, Samsung is widely rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users around the globe, and they’re not alone.

Samsung started testing its Android 17 update, otherwise known as One UI 9, back in May of this year. The stable version debuted on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Flip 8 in July, and the company announced its stable rollout to older devices would begin earlier this month. A delay behind the scenes left users waiting a bit longer, but it’s actually happening now.

That starts with Galaxy S26 devices, which are now widely receiving their Android 17 updates in regions all over the world. The update was already showing up for many in the US and South Korea, but it’s now appearing across Europe, India, and other regions as SammyGuru points out. Inbox by 9to5Google author Daniel Bader also notes that the roughly 4GB update landed on his Galaxy S26 Ultra in Canada earlier today. 

And the Galaxy S26 series is not alone.

	

SamMobile notes that stable updates are starting to appear for a host of other Galaxy devices, though right now in staggered releases and/or only for those who were previously enrolled in the beta program. Devices included in those early rollouts include Galaxy S25 series (including FE and Edge), Galaxy Z TriFold, Galaxy Z Fold 7, Galaxy Z Flip 7, and Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE.

Stay tuned as Samsung’s rollout expands – if history serves, we’ll be seeing a host of updates arriving in the coming days. Let us know in the comments if you see the update land on your device.

title: Google has fixed an issue that caused thousands of iPhone apps to crash overnight
snippet: An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied. more…
fullText:
An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied.

If you found apps on your iPhone or iPad were crashing last night, you’re not alone. Google confirmed last night that an issue with Analytics for Firebase was causing crashes when apps tried to launch. The issue was on Google’s end with an “incorrectly formatted payload” for the SDK.

You wouldn’t think of Google when a widespread crashing issue surfaces on iPhone, but Firebase is a valuable tool for developers on both Android and iOS, and is integrated into thousands of apps. The crashing issue was out of the developer’s hands and required a fix on Google’s end. The impact was huge, with some developers seeing tens of thousands of crashes – some far more – from their app’s users.

That fix has already been rolled out, Google confirmed.

	

Nick Cooke, a software engineer at Google, summarized a timeline of events:

Starting on Monday, 2026-09-28 at 17:41 US/PDT. Google Analytics for Firebase iOS+ experienced an issue causing crashes on launch due to an incorrectly formatted payload received by the SDK.

We fully rolled out a fix by Monday, 2026-09-28 at 19:52 US/PDT.

No SDK updates are required on your end to apply this fix.

Due to caching behavior, some app instances may still experience crashes for up to 4 hours after the rollout completed. These remaining cases should automatically resolve themselves by 2026-09-28 at 23:52 US/PDT.

At this point, crashing issues should be resolved. The patch for this problem was fully rolled out by around midnight Pacific Time last night; no app updates needed. Affected apps should be fully working again at this point.

fullText:
9to5Mac is brought to you by CleanMyMac by MacPaw. With the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate, use CleanMyMac first to free up space, optimize your system, and ensure your new Mac runs at 100% on day one. Learn more.

One of the many new features included in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature, which lets users get alerted when a website updates content they’re interested in. Here’s how to use it.

Safari can now notify you when webpages change

One of the most useful ways Apple has incorporated Apple Intelligence into macOS 27 Golden Gate is through Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature.

With it, users can ask Safari to monitor a webpage for specific changes and receive a notification when it detects an update.

When setting up a new custom notification, in addition to telling Safari what to look for, the user can also set a regular schedule ranging from hourly to monthly.

After the custom notification is set up, Safari will check the webpage according to the selected schedule and notify the user when it detects the requested change, such as a price drop, an item coming back in stock, changes to policies, registrations opening, or new information being added to the page.

Setting up Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature:

On Safari, go to the webpage you want to keep an eye on.

Click the Page menu button to the right of the Smart Search field.

Select “Notify Me” from the pop-up menu.

In the “What should Safari look for?” field, describe what you want. Apple Intelligence will then analyze the page’s contents to determine whether it can handle your request.

Optionally, you can set how often and when Safari should check for updates. Hourly and Daily let you choose a specific time, while Weekly and Monthly also let you choose specific days.

Click Done. Alternatively, Safari may show a Next button instead. In that case, macOS will ask for permission to send Safari notifications. You can also manage Safari notification permissions from Settings > Notifications > Safari.

Importantly, since the feature relies on Apple Intelligence, it may not be available in all languages or regions. To check the current availability status, follow this link.

snippet: TCL has launched a new “Designer Series” of TV sets running Google TV with a flush mount design and matte dispaly to help your TV blend into a room as a piece of art. more…
fullText:
TCL has launched a new “Designer Series” of TV sets running Google TV with a flush mount design and matte dispaly to help your TV blend into a room as a piece of art.

Samsung’s “The Frame” series gives your living room TV a more aesthetically appealing design, and it’s been a hit, to the point where there are now several alternatives. TCL is no stranger to that with its “NXTFRAME” series having debuted in 2024.

The new “Designer Series” continues on the same idea with a flush-mount design that sits just 1.1 inches off the wall when mounted. The mount is included in the box, but you can also purchase a separate mount on wheels. There’s no external box, either, with everything being built into the TV itself. 

TCL A300L
TCL A400U

TCL has two lineups available. 

	

The TCL A300L collection includes 55-inch, 65-inch, and 75-inch sizes (85-inch coming later) with 4K QLED panels, while the TCL A400U has better quality with 4K QD-Mini LED panels that have more dimming zones. A400U comes in 55-inch, 65-inch, 75-inch, and 85-inch sizes.

The main physical difference is that A300L supports interchangable frames to better fit into your home’s aesthetic. 

Pricing starts at $899 for both collections at Best Buy.

title: Apple Card adds new feature in iOS 27 that every card should have
snippet: iOS 27 brings a variety of new features to Apple Wallet, including one exclusive to Apple Card that I wish every card offered: a hub for all recurring transactions. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 brings a variety of new features to Apple Wallet, including one exclusive to Apple Card that I wish every card offered: a hub for all recurring transactions.

iOS 27 shows Apple Card recurring transactions in one place, making it easy to track subscriptions

Subscriptions are increasingly popular in the digital-centric world. As such, it can be easy to lose track of everything you’re subscribed to.

While plenty of apps and services offer to keep track of your subscriptions, giving third parties access to your financial info can spark privacy concerns. Fortunately, those solutions soon won’t be needed for Apple Card.

In iOS 27, the Wallet app offers a new feature for Apple Card users: a recurring transaction section.

When viewing your Apple Card in iOS 27, there’s a new ‘Recurring’ option inside the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.

Tapping this will show you a list of upcoming recurring transactions, and even lets you see them on a monthly calendar view.

I like to think I have a pretty good sense of all the things I’m subscribed to. But that takes effort. And Apple Card’s new feature makes tracking subscriptions pretty effortless.

I’m especially a fan of the calendar view, as it’s so nice getting to see at a glance exactly when each charge is expected to go through.

iOS 27 lists recurring transactions based on your Apple Card history, so it won’t always catch everything. The Wallet app has a disclaimer that states: “Dates and amounts shown are predicted based on your transaction history and may not be exact. Routine spending may incorrectly appear as recurring.”

If you do see an item that’s incorrectly marked as recurring, it’s easy to correct the error.

I really hope Apple Card inspires more credit cards and banks to copy iOS 27’s new feature. It feels like a no-brainer addition that every card should have.

Now I want to start moving all my subscriptions on to Apple Card.

title: tvOS 27 adds new reason to use profiles on your Apple TV 4K
snippet: Apple keeps improving its profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 related to app access offers another reason to use profiles. more…
fullText:
Apple keeps improving its profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 related to app access offers another reason to use profiles.

tvOS 27 lets you restrict users from launching specific apps

User profiles are a common feature of every major streaming service. They ensure viewers in a shared household can keep their viewing history and recommendations separate, among other benefits.

Apple has long had a profiles feature in tvOS, but it’s gotten a lot more useful in the past year thanks to several recent upgrades.

Now tvOS 27 has introduced another improvement. Per Apple’s official release notes:

Individual app controls in Settings let you block users from launching specific apps.

This change is clearly intended for parents. 

Profiles for children can already limit the types of content they’ll see in the Apple TV app. That’s a useful feature, but it won’t keep your child from opening a different app with no such restrictions.

	

Now though, parents can open Settings and block certain apps from being launched at all when a child’s profile is active.

It’s a good step toward making profiles as full-featured as they deserve to be, and aligns with Apple’s recent focus in iOS 27 on upgrading parental controls.

On the subject of profile improvements, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 will bring Apple’s profile system to iPhone and iPad for the first time. You can read about that change here.

title: The ultra-pocketable ‘Picco’ e-reader from Boox is now up for pre-order, $99
snippet: The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order. more…
fullText:
The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order.

The Boox Picco has really only been teased here and there. We got a preview at IFA 2026, but we didn’t get to dive in as much as we wanted. The unit was still pre-production and in need of various refinements. Still, Boox has been in this game for a while, so we expect a good experience.

Today, Boox announced that Picco is now available for pre-order on its website. It starts at $99, but the website lists it at $109 for those purchasing from the US warehouse.

The Picco’s black-and-white display comes in at just 3.97 inches, and even still, it offers a front light for day and night reading sessions. It weighs just 58 grams, and even though Boox doesn’t list the device’s thickness in the press release, our own hands-on would tell us the tiny e-reader is plenty thin.

	

It will still add a little bulk to your phone if you choose to attach it with magnets. While it isn’t magnetic by itself, the Boox Picco comes with a case that makes it possible. It’s one of the most demanded features for the tiny e-readers that have already been released, because it adds a second screen without the doomscrolling and eye strain.

Another great detail to point out during the pre-order phase is that the Boox Picco doesn’t run Android, which we covered previously. This means access to third-party apps from the Google Play Store isn’t available. Still, a simple experience will allow users to transfer files with a companion app if you don’t want to use the SD card slot to manually move ePUB files.

Boox’s adorable little Picco is expected to ship out around October for those who pre-order.

fullText:

Larger HomePod won’t be updated in October, but new version is coming ‘eventually’ per Bloomberg

Smart home hub, commonly called ‘HomePad’

New Apple TV 4K

Apple aims to eventually update its larger HomePod speaker as well.

That’s the only mention he makes of the larger HomePod product, which hasn’t been updated since 2023.

Earlier this year, Gurman reported that a new full-sized HomePod was in the works alongside the updated HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K. When asked about their arrival, he said: “Just a matter of time. But despite Siri AI officially launching, and support being ready for the HomePod mini, it seems fans of the large HomePod will have to wait a while longer for a Siri AI-compatible hardware update.

title: Report: Apple working on new Vision Pro, with different form factors on the table
snippet: After the release of Vision Pro, everyone wanted to know how long it would be before the company could release a lighter version that isn’t so bulky on your face. For the longest time, we had been looking forward to a so-called Vision Air, codenamed N100. That project was shelved last year, though the company is working on a new project with similar aspirations, per Bloomberg. more…
fullText:
After the release of Vision Pro, everyone wanted to know how long it would be before the company could release a lighter version that isn’t so bulky on your face. For the longest time, we had been looking forward to a so-called Vision Air, codenamed N100. That project was shelved last year, though the company is working on a new project with similar aspirations, per Bloomberg.

Unlike the previous N100 project, it doesn’t seem the new project, N224, is necessarily targeted at being a lower cost offering. It could instead be a successor to the current M5-based Vision Pro model, though it might still come in at a lower price while offering the flagship experience.

This new version seems relatively early in the works, with Bloomberg reporting that it could arrive between late 2028 and early 2029. That said, it isn’t quite clear what exactly Apple will be going for. The company currently has four concepts in the works.

One of the concepts is similar to the recently unveiled Meta VR glasses, which offloads the compute and battery to an external puck. Given the fact that Vision Pro already has an external battery, offloading the compute doesn’t necessarily seem like a major hurdle, though you’d need better thermals and more efficient compute to pull that off.

On the other hand, some Apple executives reportedly don’t love the idea of an external puck, and “want the company to stick with something closer to an all-in-one design.”

Design wise, Apple might get a bit more experimental compared to the current Vision Pro, with the company supposedly considering other material choices. From the Power On newsletter:

One design in testing retains the basic egg-shaped form of the current Vision Pro, but Apple is actively exploring ways to reduce its weight by experimenting with plastic, titanium, other metals and various materials. The company has also continued to explore a standalone puck that combines the computing components and battery, similar to the approach used by Meta’s recent VR Glasses.

Wrap up

Time will tell what Apple will actually end up delivering. Given the A20 Pro chip being incredibly performant at its thermal envelope, it seems highly likely that in another 2 years, we could have an A-series chip capable of running visionOS at a higher capacity than the current M5, while not needing active cooling.

	

I do think Apple should go all in on the Meta VR glasses idea. Even at a higher price point, I think the form factor makes a ton of sense. Apple silicon, EyeSight, and visionOS will allow the product stand out.

title: Apple hit with $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement
snippet: Apple must pay $5.7 billion for infringing on patents held by Taction Technology, a US jury ruled on Friday. The patents relate to Apple’s Taptic Engine, which is the hardware Apple uses to provide haptic feedback for notifications, button presses, and other interactions. Taction first filed the lawsuit in 2021, alleging Apple had “infringed and continues to infringe, directly and indirectly” its patents. more…
fullText:
Apple must pay $5.7 billion for infringing on patents held by Taction Technology, a US jury ruled on Friday. The patents relate to Apple’s Taptic Engine, which is the hardware Apple uses to provide haptic feedback for notifications, button presses, and other interactions.

Taction first filed the lawsuit in 2021, alleging Apple had “infringed and continues to infringe, directly and indirectly” its patents.

As reported by CNBC, the lawsuit centered around two patents:

U.S. Patent No. 10,659,885

U.S. Patent No. 10,820,117

Both patents are focused on a “vibration module for applying vibrational tractions to a wearer’s skin.” Taction argued that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes upon its patents, saying that Apple was “capitalizing on Taction’s innovation and success.”

Apple’s Taptic Engine first debuted as part of the Apple Watch in 2014 and came to the iPhone 6s and iPhone 6s Plus the following year, replacing the older vibration motor.

In a statement, an Apple spokesperson said:

“While we thank the jury for their consideration, we strongly disagree with today’s verdict and the damages awarded, which are entirely unsupported by the facts.

Apple’s Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction’s technology, which Taction’s own testing of Apple’s products confirmed during trial. Apple does not use Taction’s technology, and we will appeal.”

Taction Technology is a California-based company that describes itself as being “obsessed by sound.” The company says that its “Transporter Technology powers the game-changing Corsair HS60 Haptic headphones, and will soon be powering other premium headphones from major manufacturers.”

In a statement to CNBC, Taction’s lead counsel said:

“We’re happy the jury found for Taction and vindicated its patent rights. Taction waited five and a half years for this case to get to trial, so it was a long time coming.”

You can read the original complaint for patent infringement filed by Taction here and Friday’s jury ruling here.

title: Apple’s Final Cut Camera App Gets Updated for iPhone 18 Pro’s Signature Feature
snippet: The filming app adds controls for the variable aperture and shutter, giving you more ways to dial into the 18 Pro and Pro Max’s new camera features.
fullText:
Apple’s Final Cut Camera app is getting updated on Tuesday with support for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s camera, adding the ability to take advantage of the phone’s variable aperture and Cinematic mode effects.

The app update, announced in a post on Apple’s newsroom, includes a redesign that’s available for any iPhone. It provides easier access to commonly used settings like white balance and ISO, along with customizable overlays. 

		

			

But iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max owners will get the most from this update, since it provides the ability to dial in to the variable aperture — allowing you to open it widely to let in more light or to close it to focus in on closer subjects. The camera app update also unlocks Cinematic mode effects for regular video, allowing for adjustments to focus points and depth of field when editing footage in Apple’s Final Cut Pro app.

The update to the Final Cut Camera app arrives on Apple’s App Store roughly 10 days after the release of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, with both phones debuting Pro controls in the standard camera app. Thus far, that’s included preset variable aperture settings that can be toggled between, as well as shutter speed settings that let photographers experiment with lighting.

The Final Cut Camera app focuses on video recording and includes additional features like creating a Live Multicam session that connects up to four devices running the recording software. While most people will be just fine using the video recording settings in the standard camera app, Apple’s Final Cut Camera app puts a particular emphasis on professional-level video recording.

For instance, Apple recently used the iPhone 18 Pro Max to broadcast a Los Angeles Dodgers vs. San Francisco Giants baseball game. Apple also used last year’s iPhone 17 Pro Max in similar broadcast environments.

title: Still on iOS 26? You Need to Download iOS 26.7.1 Now for This Zero-Day Patch
snippet: The update patches an issue that might lead to a “sophisticated attack,” according to Apple.
fullText:
If your iPhone isn’t running iOS 27, you should download iOS 26.7.1 now to patch a zero-day flaw. Apple wrote online that this update patches a security issue on devices running iOS versions prior to iOS 27 that might have been actively exploited in an “extremely sophisticated attack.”

Zero-day exploits are newly discovered vulnerabilities with no existing protections. Updating to software versions that patch those vulnerabilities is generally the only way to guard your devices.

You can download iOS 26.7.1 now by going to Settings > General > Software Update > Update Now and following the prompts on your screen.

		

			

According to Apple’s release notes, iOS 26.7.1 patches a security issue in CoreGraphics, a framework that handles low-level, lightweight 2D renderings. Apple wrote that this issue could lead to arbitrary code execution, which could allow a third party to steal your data or hack your device for other nefarious purposes. 

“Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals,” the company wrote online. 

Apple’s description suggests this flaw was used in a targeted attack as opposed to a widespread campaign, so most people probably aren’t the intended target of this attack. However, you should still download iOS 26.7.1 to remove the possibility entirely. 

If you’re running iOS 27, you should already be protected from this issue since Apple wrote online the flaw affected iOS versions prior to iOS 27. If you are on iOS 27, I still recommend downloading iOS 27.0.1 now to give yourself the most up-to-date software.

For more on iOS, here’s what to know about iOS 27 and why you might not see iOS 27.1 on your device.

title: Samsung’s new SmartTag is smaller, longer-lasting, and works with iPhones
snippet: Samsung has announced its third-generation Bluetooth tracker, the Galaxy SmartTag 3. It combines a smaller design and improved battery life with a few new tracking and software features, including cross-OS support intended to make it easier to share tracking information with friends and family. As revealed by leaks, the SmartTag 3 has adopted a squircle design, similar to the original SmartTag but with one key difference: There's no cutout for a key ring. That means you'll have to buy one of Samsung's protective cases if you want to directly attach the tracker to keys or a carabiner. It has an IP67 rating for protection from the elements. … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Samsung has announced its third-generation Bluetooth tracker, the Galaxy SmartTag 3. It combines a smaller design and improved battery life with a few new tracking and software features, including cross-OS support intended to make it easier to share tracking information with friends and family.

As revealed by leaks, the SmartTag 3 has adopted a squircle design, similar to the original SmartTag but with one key difference: There’s no cutout for a key ring. That means you’ll have to buy one of Samsung’s protective cases if you want to directly attach the tracker to keys or a carabiner. It has an IP67 rating for protection from the elements.

The new design has benefits though. The SmartTag 3 is 35 percent smaller and 33 percent lighter than the SmartTag 2. It’s 10 percent more power-efficient too, stretching its replaceable CR2032 battery to 550 days of normal use, or 790 days in power-saving mode.

While previous Galaxy SmartTags only worked with Samsung phones, the new generation has been broadened to support iOS too. Samsung doesn’t seem to expect it’s going to win over AirTag owners, but is instead pitching this as a way to share tracking information with friends, family, or dogwalkers for help with finding lost objects or pets. We’ve reached out to Samsung to confirm if other Android phones will be supported too.

New notification alerts can be set to trigger when a SmartTag 3 moves in or out of a set area, movement detection alerts can trigger for smaller shifts, and location history helps you follow a tag’s movements. Tracking is handled by Samsung’s own Galaxy Find Network, rather than Google’s Find Hub, which launched following the release of the SmartTag 2. Once you’re within 200ft of the tracker, ultra-wideband (UWB) and Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding combine on supported phones for more precise detection.

The SmartTag 3 is launching in black and white, starting in South Korea, where it goes on sale from October 7th. A US release will follow in early November, priced at $29.99 for a single tracker and $99.99 for a four-pack. That’s the same price as the SmartTag 2, and matches Apple’s latest AirTag and Google’s new Pixel Tag.
